cases.blamed_rule: Be generous when deciding candidacy: a position is a candidate if the text before it is a coherent, renderable stretch (a noun phrase with its predicate, a clause, a parenthetical phrase that can be translated alone, a discourse phrase that can stand alone). Mark most positions between syntactic phrases rather than only a handful of "obvious" ones.

cases.proposed_rule: Candidacy must be syntax-aware: do not mark a boundary when the preceding span ends in pre-head material (possessive, title, adjective sequence, national/organizational qualifier) if a likely head noun (institution/organization/location/common-noun nucleus) appears within the next 3 tokens; treat the span as non-renderable until that head token arrives.

cases.proposed_rule: Do not mark a boundary immediately after a finite verb when that verb lacks an expressed object/complement in the preceding span and a noun phrase or clause likely serving as its complement appears within the next 4 tokens; delay the cut until the object/complement or punctuation that closes the predicate appears.

example_pair.input: Stardust will set a new all-time record for being the fastest spacecraft to return to Earth, breaking the previous record set in May of 1969.
example_pair.output: Stardust will set a new all-time record for being the fastest spacecraft to return to Earth, <SEG:85> breaking the previous record set in May of 1969 <SEG:90>.

cases.span: while the PA agrees to leave such presence only for five years
cases.evidence: Boundary scored high/kept early so the translation assigned the wrong agent/temporal scope; the duration 'for five years' disambiguates who leaves and for how long.
cases.blamed_rule: - subordinating / clause-introducing words when they end a clause in surface position: while, although, when, because, once, if, during, after, before
cases.proposed_rule: When a cut would separate a main clause from a subordinate/contrast clause (while/although/whereas/etc.) that contains scope-limiting modifiers (only, for X years, until, permanently, temporarily, exclusively), lower the confidence (demote) or withhold the boundary until the subordinate's scope token (duration/only/etc.) appears; do not let such boundaries survive tight budgets.

example_pair.input: Israel demands an ongoing military presence in the valley for ten years once an agreement is signed while the PA agrees to leave such presence only for five years.
example_pair.output: Israel demands an ongoing military presence in the valley for ten years once an agreement is signed <SEG:90> while the PA agrees to leave such presence only for five years <SEG:85>.

cases.span: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round,
cases.evidence: Model output altered token order / wording (text_modified). The prompt already forbids edits but the model still rewrote the source instead of inserting tags.
cases.blamed_rule: Insert <SEG:s> tags only. Do NOT change, correct, or paraphrase the original text in any way.
cases.proposed_rule: Strict identity enforcement: the output must be byte-identical to the original text except for inserted <SEG:s> tokens and the required single spaces. If inserting a tag at a chosen point would require changing, moving, or re-tokenizing source words or punctuation to satisfy spacing/format rules, do not choose that point — instead pick the nearest token boundary that preserves exact original characters. Never paraphrase or reorder text; prefer fewer safe tags to any edit.

example_pair.input: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.
example_pair.output: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, <SEG:70> with players usually starting on the first hole on the course <SEG:60> and finishing on the eighteenth <SEG:50>.

summary: The prompt is over-generous in candidacy without a syntactic gate, so cuts frequently appear before heads (noun or object) and before clause-scope modifiers; that produces high-contrast errors. Also the model sometimes rewrites source text despite the output-rule prohibition. Fixes: add narrow, operational syntactic checks in the candidacy pass (hold cuts until head nouns/objects or scope tokens arrive) and enforce strict identity when inserting tags.
